DAT-01.sentence: Disk encryption and KMS-managed keys protect all databases and file storage, in line with our encryption at rest standard.

DAT-02.sentence: All customer traffic uses encryption in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher, and HTTPS is enforced on every public endpoint.

DAT-04.sentence: A privacy programme exists and GDPR compliance work is in progress, with a data processing agreement drafted for some customers.

DAT-05.sentence: Backups are taken regularly and kept offsite, but restore tests are informal.

GOV-01.sentence: A written security policy covers all staff, and management approval is renewed at each annual policy review.

GOV-02.sentence: The Chief Information Security Officer is accountable for information security and leads a dedicated security team.

GOV-03.sentence: Risk assessment is carried out ad hoc, and a risk register is being rolled out for risk management.

IAM-01.sentence: Every access request is approved by the data owner on a need to know basis, and RBAC groups define standard permissions.

IAM-02.sentence: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all staff, administrators and remote access, and single sign-on is required for production tools.

IAM-03.sentence: Admin access uses a break-glass procedure, and elevated privileges are granted only for the time needed.

IAM-04.sentence: An access review takes place once a year, and deprovisioning is handled manually for some systems.

OPS-01.sentence: Security-relevant events are sent to a central SIEM for logging, and audit logs are kept for twelve months under our log retention rule.

OPS-02.sentence: A patch management process applies updates monthly, and every CVE rated critical is tracked until closed.

OPS-03.sentence: A penetration test is not performed, and no independent security testing takes place.

OPS-04.sentence: A firewall protects the production network, and network segmentation is being rolled out between environments.

PEO-01.sentence: Security awareness training is not performed, and no phishing simulation is run.

RES-01.sentence: A documented incident response plan defines roles and severity levels, and a tabletop exercise tests it every year.

RES-02.sentence: The company does not commit to notify customers of a data breach within a set time.

SDL-01.sentence: Software follows a secure development lifecycle in which every change gets a code review and SAST runs in the pipeline.

SDL-02.sentence: Change approval is required for major releases, and rollback is tested ad hoc.

TPR-02.sentence: The in-scope services hold a current certification, and an annual independent audit renews it.
